name: Pleomorphic Xanthoastrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of pleomorphic astrocytic tumor cells with lipidized xanthomatous cells
Positive GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) staining and reticulin fiber network
Cystic lesion with enhancing mural nodule on MRI
BRAF V600E mutation detected in majority of cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of pleomorphic astrocytic tumor cells with GFAP positivity is required; radiologic and molecular findings support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and imaging findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure
weakness on one side of body

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to increased intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances such as depression or anxiety
searchTerms: mood changes like sadness or worry

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
imaging: MRI showing cystic mass with enhancing mural nodule, often superficial cortical location
T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with contrast enhancement
genetic: BRAF V600E mutation present in approximately 60-70% of cases
Absence of IDH1/2 mutations differentiates from diffuse astrocytomas
other: Histopathology reveals pleomorphic, lipidized astrocytic cells with eosinophilic granular bodies
Reticulin fiber network surrounding tumor cells

distinguishingFeatures: Usually lacks pleomorphism and xanthomatous cells

redFlags: New onset of focal seizures with progressive deficits
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Kleinschmidt-DeMasters BK, et al. Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma: a clinicopathologic study of 50 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2000.
Schindler G, et al. BRAF V600E mutation in pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma. Acta Neuropathol. 2011.
